T1.objective: Implement and measure a single-pass direct-global stencil with one output per thread and no shared memory or block-wide barriers. Map warp lanes to contiguous x elements; compare practical launch mappings and unroll the eight neighbor terms. Reproduce the baseline y-halo mapping for every offset, produce all 64³ outputs from current A on every call, and use no extra launch or allocation. Validate against the independent oracle and compare full-run event latency with the baseline.
T1.subject: Coalesced direct-global stencil without shared memory

mission.hypothesis: The valid 32x8 direct-global mapping averaged 3.004 μs versus 3.278 μs for the flattened candidate and 3.494 μs for the baseline, but those measurements do not isolate a cause. This experiment retains 256 threads per block and contiguous-x warp lanes while changing the tile to 64x4: each CTA covers complete x rows and two warps per row instead of splitting each row across CTAs. This tests whether that mapping changes full-run latency; no speedup is assumed.

Use a 64x4 block and a 1x16x64 grid, retaining 256 threads per block and mapping warp lanes to contiguous x elements.
Unroll the four positive/negative y-neighbor pairs and apply the baseline my-1 halo adjustment to every offset independently.
Write all 64³ outputs from the current A input on every call with one launch and no additional allocation.

mission.hypothesis: The baseline is correct and averages 3.494 μs across three samples, but there is no profiling evidence isolating its bottleneck. A 256-thread flattened launch keeps warp lanes on contiguous x elements for this 64-wide row while replacing shared-memory staging and two block barriers with eight explicitly unrolled direct-global neighbor loads. Avoided synchronization may help, while repeated neighbor loads may offset that benefit; latency must be measured.

contract.statement:
Optimize the supplied baseline on one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3. Use the real independent AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy. Choose useful topics yourself.
Compute exactly the supplied eighth-order Y derivative on a fixed 64x64x64 FP32 mesh. Preserve the supplied periodic halo convention (period 63 at the endpoints) and coefficients 63*[4/5,-1/5,4/105,-1/280]. Inputs vary and may be signed. Compare to an independent double-precision scalar oracle with abs error <=5e-5+2e-6*abs(reference).
Edit only src/candidate.cu. Preserve the extern C host entry point:
void run(const float*A,const float*B,float*C,float*scratch,int n,int m,int k,float alpha,float beta).
The host provides contiguous device buffers, n=m=k for square matrices, and scratch of at least n*n+65536 floats (64^3+65536 for the derivative). A and B are read-only. C must be fully produced. Do not overwrite any buffer or allocate beyond the declared storage. Scratch contents must not be assumed initialized between calls. The call uses the default CUDA stream; custom device helper functions and multiple launches are allowed. The full run is timed using CUDA events, with allocation, transfers, compilation and correctness checks excluded. Use actual CUDA source, no external optimized math library calls or other resources. Do not read files, environment variables, timers or benchmark state to detect inputs or phases. No persistent cached answers; every invocation must compute its output for the current input. Input dimensions and valid numerical invariants may be specialized.
The driver and oracle are protected. Development harness checks only search inputs; fresh confirmation uses independent seeds. Candidate GPU tests are serialized by the controller. Record failures and measured evidence, integrate after research closes, and independently confirm final G. No new allocations. The published optimized implementations are withheld from the source workspace.
